title: Network dynamics of positive and negative affect in bipolar disorder

title: An investigation of emotion dynamics in major depressive disorder patients and healthy persons using sparse longitudinal networks

nlme (for multilevel VAR models)

Amelia (for multiple imputation of data points, for sparse VAR models)

notes: Uncertain about the estimation packages used, as the paper does not explicitly mention which R packages were used for network estimation. Also, it is unclear whether the authors checked for potential redundancy between nodes before running the network model.

sample_size: Low CT (n = 229); Medium CT (n = 258); High CT (n = 201); Low GL ( n = 452); Medium GL (n = 90); High GL (n = 56) - The authors looked at temporal affect data in six networks, by categorizing 3 levels each of genetic liability to psychopathology (GL) and childhood trauma (CT)

title: Metacognitive Therapy Versus Cognitive Behavioral Therapy: A Network Approach
sample_size: CBT treatment (n = 33); MCT treatment (n = 34)

estimation_packages: mlvar (0.4) - they cite the package when talking about the mlVAR method but don't explicitly say they use it
limitations: - The networks were not tested against each other using significance tests due to potential power problems;- The sample size is limited, even though normal for psychotherapy studies;- There are no implemented packages in R to estimate stability and accuracy in longitudinal networks;- Results should be replicated and compared with a validation dataset;- Future replications are needed;- Analyzing psychotherapy data using a network approach is in its early stages;- Differences between treatments could be tested in larger samples;- Items from the BAI may not be the most representative for catastrophic beliefs;- The items chosen for negative metacognitions are not representative for all aspects of metacognitions;- Other aspects of metacognition should also be investigated;- Used a t-1 lag representing a week; other relationships between nodes on other timeframes should be investigated.
notes: The paper did not specify the device used for data collection; there may be confusion regarding the visualization packages used, as they mention ggraph but reference qgraph; unsure about declaration of code availability.

title: A time-series network approach to auditory verbal hallucinations: Examining dynamic interactions using experience sampling methodology

title: Modelling suicide ideation from beep to beep: Application of network analysis to ecological momentary assessment data
limitations: - The sample included only patients with Major Depression, limiting generalizability to other diagnoses;- Sample consisted of inpatients only, possibly diminishing ecological validity;- The EMA design with ten measurements a day between 8 am and 8 pm might not capture important events occurring at other times;- Important risk factors such as defeat and entrapment were not included;- Only self-reports were used; objective measures were not included;- The design and sampling strategy may not capture the natural course of SI and its risk factors;- The study might be underpowered to detect more subtle dynamic relations;- Connections in the network should be interpreted as indications of potential causality, not definitive evidence.
notes: I was unsure whether the authors checked for redundancy between nodes before running the network model; the paper did not mention preregistration or data/code availability explicitly.

notes: I was unsure whether the authors checked for potential redundancy between nodes before running the network model. Also, it is unclear if the study was preregistered.

title: Within-person networks of clinical features of social anxiety disorder during cognitive and interpersonal therapy

title:

Independence

title: Network dynamics of momentary affect states and future course of psychopathology in adolescents
sample_size: Stable symptom levels (n = 81); Increasing symptom levels( n = 78)
limitations: - Data came from a twin sample, potentially introducing shared hereditary effects that were not addressed;- Sample was almost exclusively Caucasian, limiting generalizability;- Inclusion of emerging adults along with adolescents may affect generalizability;- Methodological decisions may have impacted results (selection of 50% with lowest happy childhood experiences, division into tertiles);- Possible exclusion of important affective experiences due to selection criteria for ESM items;- Use of SCL-90 total score may have averaged out changes in specific symptom domains;- Conservative but arbitrary threshold for differences in within-person SDs;- Simplification of random effects covariance structure;- Only two time points were assessed, limiting the developmental trajectory captured;- Analyses at group level prevent estimation of individual-level effects.
notes: I was slightly unsure about the sample type, as participants were adolescents at increased risk but not diagnosed with mental disorders.

title: Subjectifying the Personality State: Theoretical Underpinnings and an Empirical Example

title: Group and longitudinal intra-individual networks of eating disorder symptoms in adolescents and young adults at-risk for an eating disorder
sample_size: Pooled sample (n = 1272); Treatment conditions: Control condition( n = 542); Body dissonance condition (n = 495); Expressive writing condition (n = 119); Healthy weight condition (n = 116)
limitations: - Only 50 individual networks were created, which may be a small sample size;- Data was collected retrospectively and may contain recall bias error;- Data was collected over three years during an intervention, so assumption of stationarity may be violated;- Impossible to determine if individual networks are heterogeneous due to individual differences or prevention condition;- Cannot make causal claims as the study is not experimental;- Some models included only three nodes due to high heterogeneity of symptom endorsement;- Time lag was four weeks, which is longer than traditionally used in temporal networks;- Did not test if symptoms predicted onset of clinical eating disorders.
notes: I was unsure about the data collection device used, as the paper does not specify whether 'paper and pen' or 'computer' was used for the interviews.
